messages.author: eceaf8d32dda4993
messages.subject: skewed data
parts:
Hey Everyone,

I have been working through data I collected in the field and while looking through histograms I found that some of the species I recorded in my field research are highly skewed and when I run the distance R package it will not fit the data to a model. Are there any methods in which I can make the data I could run the data to get more accurate density readings for these species? Is there a way of making the data I already have fit a normal distribution curve? If it helps here is a summary of the methods I used to collect my data. I randomly selected housing sights in which I made survey sights at 20, 120, 220, and 320 meters away from the house. Once the sights were determined I would go to each sight and wait one minute to elevate any disturbance I might have caused going to the sight. From there I did a 5 minute survey in which I counted any individual bird I found within 50 meters of my current position. I recorded the species and distance way the individual was from my location. I did these surveys in the morning at sunrise to about 10 (~4 hours).

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] skewed data
parts:
Eric

What histograms are you looking at?  Are you looking at histograms of detections by distance that you create yourself, or are you looking at the scaled histogram produced when you specify plot(..., pdf=TRUE)?  Are you setting ds(..., transect="point") in your analysis?  There is no purpose in fitting a normal curve to your detections.  Have a look at the analyses of point transect data shown in

http://www.creem.st-and.ac.uk/DS.M&A/montrave/montrave-analysis.html

that mirror analyses carried out by Buckland (2006) in his Auk paper.
